status_notes: The Document Control table (PDF p. 7) lists 131.0-B-1 (September 2003), B-2 (August 2011), B-3 (September 2017) and B-4 (April 2022) as superseded. 131.0-B-5 (September 2023) is the 'Current issue'; it provides a revised pseudo-randomizer (section 10) to avoid spectral spikes on high-data-rate links. key_points.text: Issue 5 (September 2023) replaces issue 4 (April 2022); its substantive change is a revised pseudo-randomizer to avoid spectral spikes on high-data-rate links.
Scope: synchronization and channel coding for TM, AOS and USLP Transfer Frames over the CCSDS RF physical layer (401.0-B), on space-to-ground, space-to-space or ground-to-space links.
Bit numbering: Bit 0 is the first transmitted bit and the MSB of any binary field.
Frame validation uses the RS or LDPC decoder's own decision; if neither code is used, the TM/AOS/USLP Frame Error Control Field must be present.

Basic convolutional code: non-systematic, rate 1/2, K = 7, connection vectors G1 = 1111001 (171 octal) and G2 = 1011011 (133 octal), with inversion on the G2 output; punctured rates 2/3, 3/4, 5/6 and 7/8 use no inversion.
Reed-Solomon E=16 gives the (255,223) code and E=8 the (255,239) code; allowable interleaving depths are I = 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and 8, normally fixed on a Physical Channel for a Mission Phase.

The 32-bit ASM 0x1ACFFC1D is used for uncoded, convolutional, RS, concatenated, rate-7/8 LDPC and SMTF-stream LDPC data; 64-bit 0x034776C7272895B0 for rate-1/2 turbo and rate-1/2, 2/3, 4/5 LDPC; longer markers for rate-1/3, 1/4 and 1/6 turbo.
The embedded-data-stream ASM (for example frames played back inside another stream) is 0x352EF853.
The ASM is never presented to the RS, turbo or LDPC encoder or decoder, and it is not randomized.
Randomization is required unless the designer verifies proper operation without it; its presence is fixed per Physical Channel and known a priori by the receiver.

The default pseudo-random sequence is 131071 bits long, generated by h(x) = x^17 + x^14 + 1 and seeded with '11000111000111000'; the legacy 255-bit sequence h(x) = x^8+x^7+x^5+x^3+1 (all-ones seed) may still be used for backward compatibility.

Frame lengths: uncoded or convolutional-only frames may be any number of octets up to 2048 (TM/AOS) or 65536 (USLP); RS frames are L = (255-2E-q)*I octets; turbo frames are 223, 446, 892 or 1115 octets; rate-7/8 LDPC frames are 892 octets and rate-1/2, 2/3, 4/5 LDPC frames 128, 512 or 2048 octets.
All managed parameters are fixed for all Transfer Frames on a Physical Channel during a Mission Phase.
The service (Annex A) is ChannelAccess.request/indication; the receiving end gets a Quality Indicator (uncorrectable error) and a Sequence Indicator (frames lost through loss of frame sync).
The turbo-code patent (US 5,446,747, France Telecom/TDF) expired in 2012; the rate-1/2, 2/3 and 4/5 LDPC codes are covered by US Patent 7,343,539 (Caltech).

notes: PDF pages 1 and 2 are duplicate cover pages. The extraction has 101 PDF pages (registry: 100). Internal inconsistencies in the source: 2.2.2 lists 'Turbo coding (section 5)' and the note in 11.7 refers to 'Turbo Codes specified in section 5', but Turbo coding is section 6 (section 5 is Concatenated Coding). Annex E's note says 'Normative references are listed in 1.7', but they are in 1.8. Reference [E5] is called 'Mission Profiles for TM Synchronization and Channel Coding' in 2.2.2 but 'TM Channel Coding Profiles' in the list. The patent contact details in Annex B3 (names, addresses, telephone numbers, e-mail addresses) are deliberately not reproduced here. Section 1.8 references 'constitute provisions of this Recommended Standard' (kind 'normative'); Annex E lists informative references. The two patents are recorded as 'mentioned'. The SCCC (131.2-B) and DVB-S2 (131.3-B) options are only referenced, not specified, here. No individual authors are named.
